reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) directly demonstrates N-doping, M–N bond formation, and a Pt-rich shell in a PtCoFeNiCu HEA catalyst, supporting the structural and mechanistic premises. However, the evidence is from electrocatalytic ORR conditions, not automotive exhaust with H2O/NO and thermal aging, so the premise that these features will enhance durability under the specified exhaust conditions is an extrapolation not directly supported by the cited passages.
premises: N-doping induces lattice distortion and alters electronic structure, strengthening metal–N bonds that inhibit metal dissolution and corrosion.
Multiple metal–nitrogen bonds (notably Ni–N and Co–N) form synergistically to improve corrosion resistance of 3d transition metals.
A Pt-rich surface shell spontaneously segregates during N-doping, modifying adsorption energies and protecting less noble metals from leaching.
The combined effect of high entropy, multiple M–N bonds, and a Pt-rich shell enhances activity and durability.
Post-synthesis ammonia treatment at >550 °C can induce these structural features in a multi-element alloy catalyst.
